valois-0.name: Philip VI
valois-0.attire: Reconstructed long blue wool/silk royal robe, ermine-edged mantle, low open fleur-de-lis crown; early fourteenth-century silhouette.
valois-0.props: Small sceptre and sealed charter at lower edge.
valois-0.setting: Interpretive Gothic royal chamber with stone lancet window, not Versailles.
valois-0.likeness: The Saint-Denis effigy is documented by the French heritage inventory; use its idealized medieval convention, not a claim to certain facial likeness. Mature face and shoulder-length hair are reconstruction.
valois-0.avoid: Renaissance slashed doublet; late full plate harness; modern three-fleur arms replacing the earlier semy without explanation.

valois-1.name: Francis I
valois-1.attire: Broad black-and-cream slashed silk doublet, large sleeves, soft dark feathered cap, gold chain; French Renaissance court dress.
valois-1.props: Gloved hand resting on sword pommel below chest.
valois-1.setting: Interpretive Fontainebleau Renaissance pilaster and warm tapestry.
valois-1.likeness: Jean Clouet court portraits support the long nose, narrow eyes and dark short beard. Composition and room are new artistic interpretation.
valois-1.avoid: Louis XIV wig; Tudor Henry VIII's square face; generic medieval crown and mail.

valois-2.name: Catherine de’ Medici
valois-2.attire: Black widow's gown and pointed black veil, crisp white pleated ruff, restrained jewelry.
valois-2.setting: Interpretive Valois cabinet with a small collection of portrait drawings.
valois-2.likeness: The Carnavalet Clouet-workshop portrait circa 1565 documents her widow costume; the Culture Ministry describes the pointed veil and white ruff. Mature broad face interpreted from these portraits.
valois-2.avoid: Witch imagery; poison vial; Italian Renaissance dress from her youth combined with late mourning face.

valois-3.name: Charles V
valois-3.attire: Long fitted-sleeve robe, fur-lined mantle and modest open crown; fourteenth-century court silhouette.
valois-3.props: Illuminated bound manuscript held against chest.
valois-3.setting: Reconstructed Louvre library tower, wooden book bench and stone window.
valois-3.likeness: Saint-Denis identifies his lifetime effigy as an individualized portrait. BnF documents the Louvre library from 1368. Thin mature face follows the effigy tradition; colors and pose are interpretation.
valois-3.avoid: Printed modern books; spectacles invented as a personal attribute; Habsburg Charles V armor.

valois-4.name: Charles VII
valois-4.attire: Rich red velvet robe with fur trim and blue soft hat, broad shoulders.
valois-4.props: Hands quietly joined near the lower portrait boundary.
valois-4.setting: Muted drapery and late Gothic window; interpretive royal interior.
valois-4.likeness: Fouquet's circa 1450 portrait, discussed by Musée Condé, provides long nose, heavy-lidded eyes and tired, monumental expression. The new setting is not a historical scene claim.
valois-4.avoid: Beard; sixteenth-century ruff; Joan of Arc's armor transferred to the king.

valois-5.name: Louis XI
valois-5.attire: Restrained dark wool gown, fur edging and close soft cap; devotional hat badge optional.
valois-5.setting: Interpretive private chamber at Plessis with small shuttered window.
valois-5.likeness: Louvre holds later representations, including the 1838 Jaley statue; these are reception evidence rather than lifetime proof. Lean mature face and long nose are a cautious reconstruction informed by the familiar portrait tradition.
valois-5.avoid: Literal spiders or webs; sinister fantasy costume; claiming a nineteenth-century image is contemporary.

valois-6.name: Henry II
valois-6.attire: Dark fitted doublet with gold detail, short standing collar and modest white neck frill; alternatively period tournament cuirass beneath a mantle.
valois-6.props: Closed tournament helmet placed low at one side.
valois-6.setting: Interpretive Renaissance courtyard with pale stone arch.
valois-6.likeness: Louvre's Clouet-workshop portrait circa 1559 provides narrow face, cropped dark hair and pointed beard. Armor and courtyard are interpretive and must match the 1550s.
valois-6.avoid: English Henry II medieval costume; injury spectacle; seventeenth-century wig.

valois-7.name: Charles IX
valois-7.attire: Luxurious jeweled dark toque, embroidered doublet, white ruff and gold chain.
valois-7.likeness: Chantilly documents Clouet's 1570 portrait, thin moustache and beard, deliberately matured pale face. Preserve youthful age rather than generating an elderly ruler.
valois-7.avoid: Thick mature beard; gore or massacre props; Louis XIII moustache styling.

valois-8.name: Henry III
valois-8.attire: Black court doublet, high white ruff, jeweled cap, blue Order of the Holy Spirit ribbon.
valois-8.setting: Interpretive wood-paneled cabinet with candle glow.
valois-8.likeness: Rouen museum documents a late-sixteenth-century portrait after Decourt or Dumonstier with the blue Holy Spirit ribbon; narrow face and trimmed beard are portrait-tradition interpretation.
valois-8.avoid: Caricature based on sexuality; literal assassin dagger; English medieval Henry III.

valois-9.name: Marguerite de Valois
valois-9.attire: Pearled dark French court gown, structured bodice, white open ruff and carefully dressed dark hair.
valois-9.props: Closed literary manuscript with plain binding.
valois-9.setting: Interpretive Renaissance chamber with distant carved caryatid detail.
valois-9.likeness: Louvre identifies the 1572 bride of Henri de Navarre, resolving her identity. Facial details, gown colors and literary pose are plausible interpretation, not authenticated likeness from this contextual source.
valois-9.avoid: Confusion with Marguerite of Angoulême or the 1523–1574 Duchess of Savoy; eroticized Queen Margot stereotypes.

valois-10.name: Louis XII
valois-10.attire: Gold patterned long robe with rich but restrained collar; late-fifteenth-century cap or uncovered straight shoulder-length hair.
valois-10.props: Small devotional book at lower edge.
valois-10.setting: Interpretive chapel side chamber with blue fleur-de-lis textile.
valois-10.likeness: Getty's Bourdichon Hours of Louis XII, 1498/1499, is contemporary royal imagery and shows the king kneeling. Recompose its courtly silhouette into a bust; natural facial detail remains interpretation.
valois-10.avoid: Later Renaissance ruff; powdered wig; an actual saint standing behind the sitter as historical fact.

valois-11.name: Claude of France
valois-11.attire: Early-sixteenth-century French gown with square neckline, richly woven sleeves, linen underlayer and dark hood.
valois-11.props: Very small illuminated prayer book, approximately palm-sized.
valois-11.setting: Interpretive Loire royal oratory; subtle Breton ermine textile accent.
valois-11.likeness: Morgan documents her tiny 1517 prayer book, marriage and age. Young face is reconstruction rather than a claimed portrait likeness; avoid aging her beyond her death at twenty-four.
valois-11.avoid: Late Elizabethan ruff; elderly queen; giant folio substituted for her documented tiny prayer book.

valois-12.name: Isabeau of Bavaria
valois-12.attire: Burgundian-influenced French court gown with high waist, fur-lined open sleeves and period horned headdress with veil.
valois-12.setting: Interpretive textile-hung royal chamber inspired by the Book of the Queen presentation miniature.
valois-12.likeness: British Library identifies Harley 4431 as made for Isabeau; this is a stylized manuscript representation, not a verified naturalistic likeness. Mature face and gown colors are interpretation.
valois-12.avoid: Oktoberfest/Bavarian folk costume; sexualized regency caricature; late conical fairy-tale hennin.

valois-13.name: John II
valois-13.attire: Plain close-necked dark robe with contrasting mantle; fourteenth-century royal attire.
valois-13.props: Small sealed document; optional low sword hilt, not prison chains.
valois-13.likeness: BnF documents his 1354 coin and later Fouquet chronicle imagery. The familiar long-nosed profile, reddish hair and short beard may guide interpretation, but this dossier does not authenticate exact facial colors.
valois-13.avoid: Modern prisoner uniform; Renaissance armor; later chronicle imagery represented as eyewitness evidence.

bourbon-0.name: Henry IV
bourbon-0.attire: Dark early-seventeenth-century armor, white neck linen and white sash; avoid allegorical Roman armor for literal costume.
bourbon-0.setting: Interpretive pale-stone palace terrace and softened landscape.
bourbon-0.likeness: Pau describes graying hair and beard, fine wrinkles and slight smile in the circa 1605–1606 Mars portrait, and documents lifetime Pourbus portraits. Use these facial cues while treating the Mars costume as allegory.
bourbon-0.avoid: Literal Roman emperor costume; young Navarre portrait face combined with gray mature beard.

bourbon-1.name: Louis XIV
bourbon-1.attire: Dark full-bottom curled wig, lace cravat, blue-and-gold mantle with ermine lining; torso-focused royal portrait.
bourbon-1.setting: Interpretive Versailles marble and gold pilaster, subdued behind head.
bourbon-1.likeness: Versailles identifies Rigaud's 1701 state portrait and documents the king's palace patronage. Use a mature long face and prominent nose, not a young ballet dancer's face.
bourbon-1.avoid: Literal sun halo; eighteenth-century powdered side rolls; modern military medals.

bourbon-2.name: Louis XIII
bourbon-2.attire: Polished cuirass, white falling lace collar, silk sash, natural shoulder-length dark hair.
bourbon-2.props: Gloved hand and command baton low in composition.
bourbon-2.setting: Interpretive hunting lodge brick and stone, before Louis XIV's grand Versailles.
bourbon-2.likeness: NPG's later engraving after Champagne records the established portrait tradition; slender face, fine moustache and pointed beard are interpretation from that tradition, not a new eyewitness likeness.
bourbon-2.avoid: Louis XIV's enormous late wig; medieval crusader armor; completed Hall of Mirrors.

bourbon-3.name: Anne of Austria
bourbon-3.attire: Black silk regency gown, broad white lace collar, pearls and dark veil appropriate to widowhood.
bourbon-3.setting: Interpretive French palace cabinet rather than Spanish infanta nursery.
bourbon-3.likeness: Versailles's portrait teaching resource documents the queen regent and her political position. Mature rounded face and brown hair are portrait-informed reconstruction; resolve as Louis XIII's wife, not Anna of Austria wife of Philip II.
bourbon-3.avoid: Mixing up the two Austria queens in the roster; eighteenth-century panniers; poison imagery.

bourbon-4.name: Louis XV
bourbon-4.attire: Powdered curled hair, embroidered silk coat, lace cravat and blue royal sash.
bourbon-4.setting: Interpretive restrained Versailles private cabinet with delicate gilding.
bourbon-4.likeness: Versailles documents the 1763 Louis-Michel van Loo portrait. Mature oval face, powdered curls and composed expression follow that portrait tradition; room and pose are new.
bourbon-4.avoid: Louis XIV dark full-bottom wig; revolutionary dress; medieval crown as everyday wear.

bourbon-5.name: Louis XVI
bourbon-5.attire: Embroidered late-eighteenth-century coat, white lace and powdered hair tied back; blue order sash.
bourbon-5.props: Small brass lock mechanism on a table, an interpretive allusion rather than a documented sitting.
bourbon-5.setting: Interpretive Versailles private study with restrained paneling.
bourbon-5.likeness: Versailles identifies Callet's 1779 portrait and the king's dates. Broad youthful-to-middle-aged face and stout build follow state portrait tradition; the workshop prop is interpretation.
bourbon-5.avoid: Guillotine; caricature of stupidity; confusing current card role Lawgiver with actual law-book portrait evidence.

bourbon-6.name: Marie Antoinette
bourbon-6.attire: Pale blue silk gown with lace fichu and restrained ribbon trim, powdered dressed hair with modest feather or ribbon.
bourbon-6.likeness: Versailles documents her private apartments and Petit Trianon association; portrait tradition informs elongated oval face and fair hair. Rose, exact gown and scene are artistic interpretation.
bourbon-6.avoid: Cake as personality prop; gigantic novelty ship headdress; modern bridal costume; sexualized caricature.

bourbon-7.name: Marie de’ Medici
bourbon-7.attire: Rich dark silk gown, structured bodice, broad lace collar and pearl jewels; early Baroque court silhouette.
bourbon-7.props: Folded architectural drawing near lower edge.
bourbon-7.setting: Interpretive Luxembourg Palace gallery with warm marble.
bourbon-7.likeness: Louvre preserves her portrait and Rubens cycle, evidence for her represented mature face and patronage. The architectural prop and realistic room recompose this evidence; no allegorical deities.
bourbon-7.avoid: Catherine de' Medici's sixteenth-century widow hood as interchangeable identity; Roman goddess armor treated as daily attire.

bourbon-8.name: Philippe of Orléans
bourbon-8.attire: Elaborately embroidered seventeenth-century coat, fine lace cravat, dark curled wig, jeweled order ornament.
bourbon-8.setting: Interpretive Saint-Cloud salon with a garden glimpse.
bourbon-8.likeness: Versailles explicitly identifies Louis XIV's brother Monsieur and his Saint-Cloud court. Facial rendering is interpretation informed by the period portrait tradition; this is not the later Regent Philippe II (1674–1723).
bourbon-8.avoid: Regent identity swap; mockery or stereotyped costume based on sexuality; eighteenth-century powdered wig.

bourbon-9.name: Louis II de Condé
bourbon-9.attire: Seventeenth-century cuirass, white lace collar and red drapery; long natural or lightly dressed dark hair.
bourbon-9.setting: Interpretive distant campaign plain or Chantilly terrace, not nineteenth-century rebuilt château facade.
bourbon-9.likeness: Chantilly identifies Juste d'Egmont's portrait of the Grand Condé, with long hair and red drapery. Prominent aquiline nose and lean face are portrait-informed interpretation.
bourbon-9.avoid: Medieval plate suit; eighteenth-century tricorne; invented trophies of violence.

bourbon-10.name: Antoine of Bourbon
bourbon-10.attire: Refined dark doublet, small white neck frill, soft dark toque and fine gold chain.
bourbon-10.setting: Interpretive Renaissance Pau chamber with mountain light.
bourbon-10.likeness: Pau's 1557 François Clouet portrait is a contemporary source, described as a three-quarter view with penetrating gaze and refined severe costume. Short beard and facial proportions should follow this model.
bourbon-10.avoid: Henry IV's gray beard; seventeenth-century lace collar; folk Basque costume imposed on a French court prince.

bourbon-11.name: Jeanne d’Albret
bourbon-11.attire: Restrained dark court gown, white linen neck frill, close dark hood and limited jewelry.
bourbon-11.props: Small bound French-language religious book with no invented readable scripture.
bourbon-11.setting: Interpretive Pau cabinet, plain timber table and Pyrenean daylight.
bourbon-11.likeness: Musée protestant documents her 1560 conversion and independent rule; Pau documents her portrait and enamel collections. Facial details and precise costume are cautious reconstruction, not a verified sitting.
bourbon-11.avoid: Puritan costume from seventeenth-century New England; nun's habit; poison-glove legend.

bourbon-12.name: Philip V of Spain
bourbon-12.attire: Armor beneath embroidered coat, red waist sash, Golden Fleece and blue Saint-Esprit sash; curled wig.
bourbon-12.props: Ruler's baton with helmet low at side.
bourbon-12.setting: Interpretive Spanish royal stone terrace, not flamenco or bullfighting scenery.
bourbon-12.likeness: Prado's Jean Ranc official portrait of 1723 explicitly documents armor, baton, helmet, embroidered coat and both orders. Recompose its mature long face and courtly stance into the card crop.
bourbon-12.avoid: Philip IV Velázquez moustache/black golilla costume; modern Spanish flag; seventeenth-century Habsburg identity.

bourbon-13.name: Louis XVIII
bourbon-13.attire: Dark high-collared embroidered coat, white stock, royal sash and period order star; short gray hair.
bourbon-13.props: Folded charter or dispatch resting on table.
bourbon-13.setting: Interpretive Restoration palace study, not a claim that he resumed residence at Versailles.
bourbon-13.likeness: Versailles documents his Restoration and Guérin's 1820 portrait. Elderly broad face and substantial build are portrait-informed; charter pose is interpretation. Versailles also says he abandoned plans to return there.
bourbon-13.avoid: Louis XIV wig; medieval costume; implying an actual coronation, which never occurred; caricaturing body size.
